Hi Lena, Marcus and team —

I'm really sorry to drop this on short notice, but I just received a mandatory jury summons for today. The court emailed me at 10:30 AM and the required arrival window overlaps the interview. I called the courthouse and the clerk confirmed the panel could be in-session unpredictably this afternoon. I can request deferral but that process is not guaranteed to be resolved today.

Options I'm proposing (happy to follow whichever is best for you):
1) Spread the loop across two shorter remote sessions tomorrow morning and Friday morning (I can do 60m each).
2) Proceed with today's schedule if you can accept a recorded session for the two live interviews I miss (I would sign any consent form).
3) Switch the system-design slot to a short take-home exercise (deliverable by EOD tomorrow) + keep any live conversations you can.

Terribly sorry — I want to make this as low friction as possible.

Thanks for understanding,
Victor
victor.ramos+candidate@example.com

Thanks for flagging, Victor — appreciate the heads up.

Team — quick coordination: jury duty is non-negotiable; we need an alternative that keeps momentum without causing extra churn. My read: option 3 (short take-home for system design + keep live chats where possible) is the fastest to preserve decision velocity.

Proposed plan (doable today/tomorrow):
- Today: cancel on-site travel; we will not request recordings of any court session.
- Take-home: Victor will complete a 90-minute system-design prompt (deliver by 5 PM PT tomorrow). We will use that to substitute the 2:00–2:45 design interview.
- Live interviews: Grace and Mina, can you do a 45-minute remote window tomorrow 10:00–11:30 AM PT? If not, earliest availability?
- Stephanie, can you approve a short consent line (one-paragraph) to confirm Victor is okay with any interview recordings if we need them?

Attachments: panel_availability_grid.xlsx (I've prefilled potential windows for tomorrow and Friday).

If we get unanimous agreement, I'll send Victor a concise take-home + revised schedule.

— Marcus
